note: Values with estimated=true are game values (1-5 scale), not real measurements. Sources in docs/FUENTES_NASA.md.

rocks.name: CHEYAVA FALLS
rocks.composition: Mud with hematite, calcium sulfate veins, olivine
rocks.water_text: Deposited as mud in water; later fluids formed the calcium sulfate veins.
rocks.description: Reddish arrowhead-shaped rock with white veins and "leopard spots": small light spots with black rims. A potential biosignature, not proof of life.

rocks.name: SÉÍTAH
rocks.location: Séítah unit, floor of Jezero crater
rocks.composition: Tightly packed olivine crystals, interstitial material
rocks.water_text: Igneous rock later altered by fluids (Tice et al., 2022).
rocks.description: Green and dark grey olivine grains that settled as a magma slowly cooled.

rocks.name: ROCHETTE
rocks.water_text: Its salts show long contact with groundwater that later evaporated.
rocks.description: Fine-grained dark grey basalt. Perseverance's first two samples came from this rock.

rocks.name: BROOM POINT
rocks.location: Witch Hazel Hill, rim of Jezero crater
rocks.composition: Angular fragments, rock dust, glass spherules
rocks.water_text: Some layers seem formed by fast flows that could point to water or ice.
rocks.description: Rock of light and dark fragments with glass spherules from asteroid impacts on early Mars.

rocks.name: SINGITA
rocks.location: Lac de Charmes, outside Jezero's western rim
rocks.age: Possibly among the oldest on Mars
rocks.water_text: Formed deep underground; no published data on water alteration.
rocks.description: Light mottled rock with "cowhide" patches. It formed ~1 km deep and an impact brought it to the surface. Extremely hard.

rocks.name: BASALT
rocks.type: Fine-grained volcanic rock · like the Máaz formation
rocks.water_text: Not analyzed. Basalts in this area carry salts from ancient groundwater.
rocks.description: Dark fine-grained volcanic rock, the most common one on the floor of Jezero.

rocks.name: OLIVINE CUMULATE
rocks.type: Olivine-rich igneous rock · like the Séítah unit
rocks.water_text: Not analyzed. Similar rocks from Séítah were altered by fluids.
rocks.description: Greenish and dark grains formed as a magma slowly cooled, like the rocks of the Séítah unit.

rocks.name: MUDSTONE
rocks.water_text: Not analyzed. Its look suggests mud deposited in water.
rocks.description: Reddish rock of hardened mud, formed in Jezero's ancient lake or river.

rocks.name: IMPACT BRECCIA
rocks.type: Rock fragments welded by an impact
rocks.water_text: Not analyzed. Formed by an impact, not in water.
rocks.description: A mix of rock pieces broken and welded together by an asteroid impact.

rocks.name: GABBRO
rocks.water_text: Not analyzed. Formed deep underground, no visible signs of water.
rocks.description: Light mottled rock that cooled slowly underground and reached the surface through an impact.
